## Verified live evidence

At main 996313a99bf7df942111cac40b8ada53107dcfe5:

- pm contracts --json --full returns only output_budget_exceeded and read_output.
- output_budget_exceeded.omitted_result is true and reason is requested_budget_infeasible.
- pm --output-budget unbounded contracts --json --full returns 26 top-level keys, 131 commands, and 104 actions.

## Contract decision required

The implementation must distinguish three cases:

1. explicit complete-result intent with no explicit budget: completeness wins;
2. explicit caller budget: the caller's cost ceiling wins and any omission is disclosed;
3. whole-result omission: this is a failed read, not a successful bounded projection, and must not be parseable as plausible domain data.

This rule belongs in the shared SDK read-output primitive, not as a contracts-only bypass.

## Regression lineage

GH-1012 and the closed resumability lineage fixed complete-result handling on list-all. The same semantic class now appears on contracts --full, proving the behavior needs a cross-surface invariant.

GH-1030: contracts --json --full is wholly omitted by the default output budget

The explicit complete-contract request pm contracts --json --full deterministically returns only a well-formed output-budget receipt under the default budget. Because stdout remains valid JSON and the actual contract is wholly omitted, downstream consumers can silently interpret missing command/action arrays as empty and publish structurally valid but content-free artifacts.

harness:codex

Reproduce the exact contracts failure in SDK and CLI tests; define an SDK-native precedence rule where explicit complete-result intent defeats an implicit default ceiling while explicit caller budgets still win; make any unavoidable omitted_result=true outcome parser-visible through deterministic nonzero exit and transport semantics; apply the class-wide rule to CLI, SDK, and MCP; add negative controls for bounded partial degradation versus whole-result omission; manually verify packed npm, npx, Bun, and bunx consumers in temporary directories; document recovery and compatibility.
project management = context management
Make explicit whole-result reads semantically complete and make whole-result omission impossible to confuse with successful empty data.
Contract generators and agents can trust that --full means complete without carrying command-specific budget folklore.
Downstream docs and integrations can silently regenerate zero-command artifacts while JSON parsing and process health remain green.
Whole-result intent precedence and omitted_result failure semantics are enforced once in the SDK read-output layer and regression-gated across every complete-result surface.
The regression is present in the current immutable daily release and has already produced an externally visible zero-command documentation artifact according to GitHub #1030.

Reproduced on repository main 996313a99bf7df942111cac40b8ada53107dcfe5 and pm-cli 2026.8.15; Linux; default output budget

Run pm contracts --json --full and inspect top-level keys. Observe only output_budget_exceeded and read_output with omitted_result=true. Run pm --output-budget unbounded contracts --json --full and observe the complete contract payload.

An explicit --full whole-surface read returns the complete contract by default, or fails in a parser-visible way before a consumer can mistake a well-formed receipt for an empty contract. CLI, SDK, and MCP expose one precedence rule and one failure contract.

The default invocation returns a successful, parseable JSON receipt with the entire result omitted. Live repository reproduction returned two receipt keys; the unbounded recovery returned 26 top-level keys, 131 commands, and 104 actions.
